review_candidates.title: AI & BI Engineering Intern
review_candidates.description: About Drop Me: Drop Me is building AI-native circular recovery infrastructure that connects smart recycling machines, digital experiences, operational systems, rewards, and environmental data. Every interaction can generate useful signals: Machine → Material → User → Location → Operations → Rewards → Business → Impact Our AI & BI function exists to turn those signals into better decisions, better automation, and more intelligent products. We are looking for an AI & Business Intelligence Intern who wants to work across applied AI, data, analytics, and decision intelligence — not only build isolated models or dashboards. The Role : You will help transform Drop Me data into: Prediction, Detection, Automation, Insight, Decision Support, and Business Intelligence. You may work with data coming from: Reverse Vending Machines. Computer vision systems. Sensors. User transactions. Green Wallet activity. Rewards. Operations. Locations. Recycling activity. Commercial partnerships. Dashboards. Internal business systems. Your work should ultimately answer: What is happening? Why is it happening? What is likely to happen next? What should we do about it? What You Will Work On: Data Understanding & Quality Before building AI, you need to understand the data. You will help: Explore Drop Me datasets. Understand data sources and business meaning. Detect missing, duplicated, or inconsistent records. Validate timestamps, IDs, quantities, and statuses. Define useful data-quality checks. Document important fields and definitions. Distinguish measured data from calculated or estimated values. 2. Business Intelligence & Dashboards You will help turn operational and commercial data into useful decision tools. This may include dashboards for: RVM performance. Material recovery. Machine uptime. Fill levels. Location performance. User engagement. Rewards activity. Operations. Commercial partners. Sustainability / ESG indicators. You will help define: KPIs, Filters, Drill-downs, Alerts, Comparisons, Trends, and Decision thresholds. A dashboard should not simply display numbers. It should help someone decide what to do next. 3. Applied AI & Machine Learning Depending on the project, you may contribute to: Classification. Anomaly detection. Forecasting. Predictive maintenance. Fraud detection. Behavioural segmentation. Recommendation systems. Pattern detection. Operational optimisation. Computer vision support. Intelligent prioritisation. You will be expected to understand: Problem → Data → Baseline → Model → Evaluation → Deployment Logic → Monitoring We do not need AI where a simple rule solves the problem better. 4. Predictive Ops One important area is using data to improve how the RVM network operates. Examples may include predicting: When a machine will become full. When collection should be scheduled. Which machines may require maintenance. Which locations are underperforming. Material-volume trends. Operational anomalies. Unusual transaction patterns. 5. User & Behaviour Intelligence You may help analyse how users interact with Drop Me. This could include: Usage frequency, Session patterns, Repeat behaviour, Reward engagement, Referral behaviour, Location preferences. Competition participation, Drop-off patterns, Cohorts, Segmentation. The objective is not to label users unnecessarily. It is to understand behaviour well enough to improve the experience. 6.AI Agents & Intelligent Automation You may help explore or build AI-assisted workflows that support Drop Me teams. Examples may include: Operational copilots. Automated reporting. Internal knowledge assistants. Dashboard insight generation. Incident summaries. Data-quality agents. Commercial intelligence. Partner reporting. Customer-support intelligence. Automated anomaly investigation. Any AI agent should have: clear purpose, controlled access, defined tools, human approval where needed, logging, and measurable value. 7. Analytics & Decision Support You will support teams by converting data into actionable analysis. Questions may include: Which RVM locations perform best? Why is one machine underperforming? Which operational issue has the highest impact? Are users returning after their first interaction? Which reward mechanics drive engagement? What is changing week over week? Which metric deserves immediate attention? What should management investigate next? You should become comfortable moving from: Data → Observation → Explanation → Recommendation 8.Data Visualisation You may create or improve: Charts. KPI cards. Trend views. Heatmaps. Funnels. Cohort views. Operational dashboards. Executive summaries. Automated reports. 9.AI Model Evaluation You will help test whether an AI solution actually works. This may include: Accuracy. Precision / Recall. F1 score. False positives. False negatives. Latency. Error analysis. Drift. Business impact. Operational cost. 10. Data Pipelines & Integration Depending on your level, you may support: Data ingestion. API integration. Database queries. ETL / ELT workflows. Cleaning pipelines. Scheduled jobs. Data transformations. Feature preparation. Analytics-ready datasets. You may work with engineering teams to understand how data moves from: RVM / App / API → Database → Analytics → Dashboard / AI 11. Monitoring & Continuous Improvement AI and analytics systems must remain trustworthy after launch. You may help monitor: Model performance. Data drift. Missing data. Broken pipelines. Dashboard anomalies. Unexpected changes. Data latency. Prediction quality. A model that worked three months ago is not automatically still working today. 12.Documentation You will be expected to document: Data sources. KPI definitions. Assumptions. Models. Experiments. Evaluation results. Queries. Pipelines. Dashboard logic. Limitations. Someone else should be able to understand why an output exists and how it was produced. Tools You May Work With Depending on the project: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, SQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Jupyter, Power BI, Looker Studio, Excel / Google Sheets, Matplotlib, Plotly, FastAPI / APIs, Git / GitHub, Docker, ML / LLM APIs, AI agent frameworks, Vector databases, Cloud services You are not expected to know every tool. We care more about your ability to learn and choose the right tool for the problem. AI / LLM Engineering Exposure You may also work with modern AI systems including: LLM APIs, Prompt design, Structured outputs, Tool calling, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Embeddings, Vector search, Agent workflows, Evaluation frameworks, Guardrails, Human-in-the-loop systems. Using an LLM is easy. Building a system that produces reliable, measurable, and controlled outcomes is the real challenge. Data Responsibility You may work with operational, business, or user-related information. You will be expected to: Use only authorised datasets. Follow access-control rules. Avoid unnecessary personal-data exposure. Never upload confidential data to unapproved tools. Protect API keys and credentials. Use anonymised or aggregated data where appropriate. Follow Drop Me security and privacy requirements. What Good Performance Looks Like During the internship, we expect you to progress toward being able to: Understand a business problem before choosing an AI model. Explore a dataset independently. Detect basic data-quality problems. Write useful SQL queries. Build clear dashboards. Define meaningful KPIs. Build a baseline before testing advanced AI. Evaluate models properly. Explain model errors. Translate analysis into a business recommendation. Automate repetitive analytical work. Document your assumptions. Challenge misleading conclusions. Communicate technical findings to non-technical teams. What We Are Looking For You may come from: Artificial Intelligence, Computer Science, Data Science, Data Engineering, Business Intelligence, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Statistics, Mathematics. Another relevant technical discipline. You should have: Analytical thinking, Curiosity, Basic programming ability, Comfort working with data, Attention to detail, Willingness to investigate problems, Good logical reasoning, Ability to explain findings clearly, Strong learning ability, Good documentation habits. Useful Technical Foundations Experience in some of the following is valuable: Python, SQL, Data cleaning, Exploratory Data Analysis, Machine Learning fundamentals, Statistics, Power BI or similar BI tools, APIs, Git, Databases, Basic cloud concepts. AI Use During the Internship AI tools are encouraged where they improve productivity. You may use them for: Code assistance, Research, Debugging, Analysis, Query generation, Documentation, Model exploration, Agent development. But you remain responsible for: Verifying the code, Verifying the numbers, Testing assumptions, Understanding the output, Protecting confidential data, Identifying hallucinations, Rejecting technically incorrect recommendations. You should be able to explain any important work you submit even if AI helped produce it. How You Will Work With the Team You may collaborate with: AI / BI, Backend Engineering, DevOps, Frontend Engineering, Product, Operations, Growth, Partnerships, Management. This means your work may begin as a data problem but eventually affect: a dashboard, an operational decision, an RVM, a customer experience, a commercial report, or an AI agent. This Role Is Probably Not for You If You mainly want to: Train models without understanding the business problem. Build dashboards without knowing who uses them. Copy notebook tutorials. Report accuracy without analysing errors. Treat correlation as causation. Trust every AI-generated result. Ignore data quality. Avoid SQL or data exploration. Present numbers without understanding their definitions. Build complicated AI where simple logic would work better. What You Can Learn Here You may gain exposure to: Applied AI, Business Intelligence, Data Analytics, Machine Learning, AI Agents, Computer Vision Data, Predictive Operations, RVM Analytics, Behaviour Intelligence, Fraud Detection, Data Visualisation, Dashboard Engineering, Data Pipelines, Model Evaluation, AI Governance, Operational Decision Intelligence.

Predictive maintenance. Fraud detection. Behavioural segmentation. Recommendation systems. Pattern detection. Operational optimisation. Computer vision support. Intelligent prioritisation. You will be expected to understand: Problem → Data → Baseline → Model → Evaluation → Deployment Logic → Monitoring We do not need AI where a simple rule solves the problem better. 4. Predictive Ops One important area is using data to improve how the RVM network operates. Examples may include predicting: When a machine will become full. When collection should be scheduled. Which machines may require maintenance. Which locations are underperforming. Material-volume trends. Operational anomalies. Unusual transaction patterns. 5. User & Behaviour Intelligence You may help analyse how users interact with Drop Me. Partner reporting. Customer-support intelligence. Automated anomaly investigation. Any AI agent should have: clear purpose, controlled access, defined tools, human approval where needed, logging, and measurable value. 7. Analytics & Decision Support You will support teams by converting data into actionable analysis. Questions may include: Which RVM locations perform best? Why is one machine underperforming? Which operational issue has the highest impact? Are users returning after their first interaction? Which reward mechanics drive engagement? What is changing week over week? Which metric deserves immediate attention? What should management investigate next? You should become comfortable moving from: Data → Observation → Explanation → Recommendation 8.Data Visualisation You may create or improve: Charts. KPI cards. Trend views. Heatmaps. Funnels. Cohort views. Operational dashboards. Executive summaries. Automated reports. 9.AI Model Evaluation You will help test whether an AI solution actually works. This may include: Accuracy. Precision / Recall. F1 score. False positives. False negatives. Latency. Error analysis. Drift. Business impact. Operational cost. 10. Data Pipelines & Integration Depending on your level, you may support: Data ingestion. API integration. Database queries. ETL / ELT workflows. Cleaning pipelines. Scheduled jobs. Data transformations. Feature preparation. Analytics-ready datasets. You may work with engineering teams to understand how data moves from: RVM / App / API → Database → Analytics → Dashboard / AI 11. Monitoring & Continuous Improvement AI and analytics systems must remain trustworthy after launch. You may help monitor: Model performance. Data drift. Missing data. Broken pipelines. Dashboard anomalies. Unexpected changes. Data latency. Prediction quality. A model that worked three months ago is not automatically still working today. 12.Documentation You will be expected to document: Data sources. KPI definitions. Assumptions. Models. Experiments. Evaluation results. Queries. Pipelines. Dashboard logic. Limitations. Someone else should be able to understand why an output exists and how it was produced. Tools You May Work With Depending on the project: Python, Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, SQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Jupyter, Power BI, Looker Studio, Excel / Google Sheets, Matplotlib, Plotly, FastAPI / APIs, Git / GitHub, Docker, ML / LLM APIs, AI agent frameworks, Vector databases, Cloud services You are not expected to know every tool. We care more about your ability to learn and choose the right tool for the problem. AI / LLM Engineering Exposure You may also work with modern AI systems including: LLM APIs, Prompt design, Structured outputs, Tool calling, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Embeddings, Vector search, Agent workflows, Evaluation frameworks, Guardrails, Human-in-the-loop systems. Data Responsibility You may work with operational, business, or user-related information. You will be expected to: Use only authorised datasets. Follow access-control rules. Detect basic data-quality problems. Write useful SQL queries. Build clear dashboards. Define meaningful KPIs. Build a baseline before testing advanced AI. Evaluate models properly. Explain model errors. Translate analysis into a business recommendation. Automate repetitive analytical work. Document your assumptions. Challenge misleading conclusions. Communicate technical findings to non-technical teams. Another relevant technical discipline. How You Will Work With the Team You may collaborate with: AI / BI, Backend Engineering, DevOps, Frontend Engineering, Product, Operations, Growth, Partnerships, Management.
